entities.summary: Pope Clement X, born Emilio Bonaventura Altieri, was head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 29 April 1670 to his death on 22 July 1676. As a member of the powerful Altieri family, he was appointed Cardinal-Priest of the Santa Maria in Minervino on 19 March 1652, and later became Cardinal-Priest of the Santa Maria del Popolo in 1662. Clement X played a key role in the Great Schism of 1689-1692, a major controversy within the Catholic Church that threatened its unity. He also supported the establishment of the Society of Jesus, founded by Ignatius of Loyola, and worked to reform the Church's financial and administrative systems. Clement X's papacy was marked by significant diplomatic efforts, including the Treaty of Nijmegen in 1678, which ended the Nine Years' War between France and the Dutch Republic. His legacy is also tied to the development of the Congregation of the Sacred Heart, a major Catholic order founded in 1679 by Jean-Jacques Olier. Clement X's contributions to the Church and his efforts to reform its structures continue to influence Catholicism today. The Pope's papacy was cut short by his death on 22 July 1676, but his impact on the Church's history is undeniable. Despite his relatively short tenure, Clement X left a lasting legacy that continues to shape the Catholic Church's development.
